open_questions: Mo's Irish Pub Sunday hours are not published on its website (its site lists Mon-Thu and Fri-Sat only, and conflicts on Fri-Sat close: midnight in one section, 2 AM in another). It is hosting the official Sunday after-party (Armchair Boogie), so it will be open late Sunday, but confirm by phone: 414-272-0721.

Cover charge / door price for the Houseplant (Fri, Sat) and Armchair Boogie (Sun) after-parties at Mo's Irish Pub is not published; they were sold as a checkout add-on with Widespread Panic tickets on pabsttheatergroup.com and listed on Discotech at 11:45 PM start. Door availability unknown.
Yelp photo URLs use best-guess business slugs and were not verified to resolve.

The Wolph free street party page lists 'doors 12:00 PM, show 5:30 PM' each day; the exact spot on Wisconsin Ave (in past years it was the closed block directly outside the Riverside) was not stated for 2026.

No urgent-care clinic with published weekend hours was found inside the immediate Westown/East Town core; the nearest confirmed is Aurora Urgent Care at Schlitz Park (1575 N RiverCenter Dr), ~1 mile north. Hours came from a third-party directory and should be confirmed by phone: 414-276-4242.

No pharmacy in downtown proper is open 24 hours. The Walgreens at 1400 E Brady St is a 24-hour STORE but its pharmacy counter opens at 8 AM. The nearest truly 24-hour pharmacy counter is Walgreens 4296 S 76th St, Greenfield (~20 min by car).

Wikimedia Commons image URLs for East Town, Historic Third Ward and Deer District were verified via the Commons API; the 1200px thumbnail links follow Wikimedia's standard pattern but could not be HEAD-checked due to API rate limiting. No images were sourced for Westown, Brady Street, Walker's Point or Bay View.

this_weekend_headline.note: Three things collide downtown this weekend: the sold-out Widespread Panic run at the Riverside (doors 6:30 PM, show 8:00 PM Saturday and Sunday), the Brewers hosting World Series Game 2 at American Family Field (7:00 PM Saturday), and Halloween-weekend parties. Every bar within a half mile of the Riverside will be loud and full from about 5 PM on Saturday. Reserve where possible (SafeHouse, Blu) and lean on the official Panic street party and after-parties, which are built for this crowd.

wsp_official_parties.name: Wolph: Free Street Party Before Widespread Panic
wsp_official_parties.address: W Wisconsin Ave outside the Riverside Theater, 116 W Wisconsin Ave, Milwaukee, WI 53203
wsp_official_parties.blurb: Pabst Theater Group's free outdoor pre-party on Wisconsin Avenue right outside the Riverside, all three nights. Wolph is a young Grateful Dead-leaning jam band whose originals are being produced by Panic's own Dave Schools, so the lot is a family affair. Doors 12:00 PM, music 5:30 PM, then straight into the theater at 6:30.
wsp_official_parties.when: Sat Oct 24, Sun Oct 25 2026: doors 12:00 PM, show 5:30 PM

wsp_official_parties.name: Official Widespread Panic After-Parties at Mo's Irish Pub
wsp_official_parties.blurb: Half a block west of the Riverside doors. Houseplant plays Saturday, Madison jamgrass quartet Armchair Boogie plays Sunday. Listed as 21+, starting 11:45 PM, which is the minute the Riverside lets out. This is the room where the whole run ends up.
wsp_official_parties.when: Sat Oct 24: Houseplant; Sun Oct 25: Armchair Boogie. Start ~11:45 PM.

bars.name: Mo's Irish Pub (Downtown)
bars.blurb: Not a craft-cocktail room, but for three nights a year it is the most important bar in Milwaukee: the official Panic after-party, 150 feet from the Riverside doors. Irish pub bones, a big stage, and a crowd that just walked out of the same show.
bars.vibe: Big, loud, friendly Irish pub that turns into a jam-band clubhouse during the Panic run. A mini-Shakedown often forms on the sidewalk outside.
bars.signature_drink: Guinness or a local tap (Lakefront, Third Space); this is a pint place, not a cocktail place
bars.wsp_fan_note: Fan guides have called Mo's 'ground zero' for pre- and post-Panic activity since at least 2014, and in 2026 it is the venue-sanctioned after-party: Houseplant Saturday, Armchair Boogie Sunday, ~11:45 PM start, 21+.

bars.name: SafeHouse
bars.blurb: A spy-themed bar hidden behind an unmarked red door on a side street, open since 1966. Entry takes a password, and without it 'Agent Moneypenny' runs a clearance test while the whole bar watches on camera. Committed kitsch, a 4-minute walk from the Riverside, and I know it only by reputation, which is sixty years long.
bars.vibe: Dim, gadget-filled, secret passages and a spinning bookcase exit. Touristy in the best way. Go early, before the show, when the crowd is lighter.
bars.signature_drink: The Spy's Demise (a tall, boozy rum punch that comes with a warning)
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan gathering spot, it is a Milwaukee rite of passage. Saturday nights often have a wait without an OpenTable reservation, so book a 4:30-5:30 PM slot and walk to the street party afterward.

bars.name: Blu at The Pfister Hotel
bars.address: 424 E Wisconsin Ave, 23rd Floor, Milwaukee, WI 53202
bars.blurb: Twenty-three floors above the city in the 1893 Pfister, with floor-to-ceiling views of downtown and Lake Michigan. Martinis, a deep wine list, live piano or jazz Friday and Saturday from 8 PM. Open until 2 AM Fri and Sat, which makes it the classiest nightcap after the show, a straight 8-minute walk east on Wisconsin Avenue.
bars.vibe: Hushed, grown-up, glittering. The lake is black at night but the city lights and the Allen-Bradley clock glow to the south. The lobby below holds the largest collection of Victorian art of any hotel in the world, and a resident ghost.
bars.signature_drink: A classic martini (Blu bills itself as one of the city's most popular martini bars)
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan bar. A good escape hatch if Mo's is too packed, 5 minutes on foot from Mo's.

bars.name: Mader's Knight's Bar
bars.address: 1041 N Old World 3rd St (now signed N Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr), Milwaukee, WI 53203
bars.blurb: The bar inside Milwaukee's most famous German restaurant (since 1902), guarded by two suits of armor in the window and hung with medieval weaponry. A boot of German lager here before the show is the most Milwaukee thing within a 10-minute walk of the theater.
bars.vibe: Dark wood, armor, steins, old-world Bavarian theater. Shares the block with Usinger's sausage (1880) and the Wisconsin Cheese Mart, so a pre-show wander up Old World Third is a greatest-hits tour of old Milwaukee.
bars.signature_drink: German draft lager (Spaten, Hofbrau) or a Wisconsin brandy old fashioned
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan bar, and it closes before the show lets out. Pre-show only.

bars.name: Bryant's Cocktail Lounge
bars.blurb: Milwaukee's oldest cocktail lounge (1938) and one of the great bars in America: no menu, no visible bottles, just velvet, low light and a bartender who asks what you like and builds something from a house repertoire of hundreds of drinks. Open until 2 AM Friday and Saturday, a 10-minute rideshare south of the Riverside. I have not sat at that bar. I have read enough people who have to trust the velvet.
bars.vibe: Mid-century lounge frozen in amber: red velvet, a jukebox, hushed conversation, no TVs. First-come seating at the bar and main lounge. The upstairs Velvet Lounge takes reservations Fri/Sat for parties of 2-8.
bars.signature_drink: Whatever the bartender makes you after you say 'something with gin, not too sweet'; the Pink Squirrel (ice-cream drink) is a Milwaukee classic they do beautifully
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan bar, which is exactly why it works as the decompression room after the Riverside. Sunday closes at midnight, so it is a Saturday after-show call.

bars.name: At Random
bars.blurb: A 1964 Bay View time capsule of Naugahyde booths, swag lamps and ice-cream cocktails, saved and run by the same owner as Bryant's. A Grasshopper or a Brandy Alexander the size of your head, in a room that looks like a Wes Anderson set. Fri/Sat open until 2 AM.
bars.vibe: Supper-club kitsch at its finest: dark, red, intimate, and strictly for people who want to talk. Groups capped at 8, first-come seating.
bars.signature_drink: Ice cream drinks: Grasshopper, Pink Squirrel, Brandy Alexander; the shareable Love Bowl for two
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan bar. Pairs with Lost Whale (a 5-minute walk away) for a Bay View after-show double.

bars.name: Lost Whale
bars.blurb: Bay View's best modern cocktail bar: tropical-leaning, sustainability-minded, zero pretension, with a serious tap-cocktail program and $4.50 old fashioneds. For October it is wearing a costume: the horror-themed Black Lagoon pop-up takes over the room all month, which suits the weekend before Halloween.
bars.vibe: Creative, casual, a little nautical, a little weird. Crowd skews 25-40, the music is good, the bartenders are friendly. That is the word from people who go, not from me.
bars.signature_drink: Tap cocktails; the seasonal Black Lagoon menu through Oct 31 (per OnMilwaukee)
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan bar. Sunday closes at 10 PM, so Black Lagoon is a Saturday after-show move (or a Sunday afternoon one).

bars.name: Boone & Crockett
bars.blurb: 'Pretentious drinks without the pretentiousness': a taxidermy-and-string-lights cocktail bar on the Kinnickinnic River in Walker's Point, with a big waterfront patio, Taco Moto on site, and a 2 AM close every night it is open. The Trinidad Sour alone is worth the 25-minute riverwalk south.
bars.vibe: Hunting-lodge-meets-dive, boats docked outside, DJs and dancing some nights, a tiki-adjacent back bar. Lively, young, fun.
bars.signature_drink: Trinidad Sour (Angostura, rye, lemon, almond) or the Gin Bramble
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not an official fan bar, but one of the few quality cocktail rooms open until 2 AM on Sunday, which makes it the closing-night nightcap.

bars.name: Wolski's Tavern
bars.blurb: A 1908 corner tavern on a residential street two blocks off Brady, run by the founder's great-grandsons. Steel-tip darts, bar dice, a popcorn machine, Stoli Orange shots, cash only. Stay until last call and the bartender hands over the 'I Closed Wolski's' bumper sticker, which cannot be bought and has been spotted from Dublin to Osaka. I have never closed Wolski's. The sticker gets around more than I do.
bars.vibe: The platonic Milwaukee corner bar: Tiffany lamps, Polish flag over the men's room, regulars who have been coming for 40 years, and zero attitude toward newcomers.
bars.signature_drink: A Miller High Life and a Stoli Orange shot (the house shot)
bars.wsp_fan_note: Fan guides have recommended it for years ('stay until closing for the bumper sticker'). Bring cash. Sunday close is 2:00 AM, so closing Wolski's on Sunday night means staying until 2.

bars.name: Von Trier
bars.blurb: A dark, carved-wood German bierstube on the East Side (here since 1978, a tavern since Prohibition's end) with 30 taps heavy on German imports, a Cyril Colnik chandelier rescued from the Pabst Mansion, hand-painted murals and a beer garden out back. When the city threatened to turn it into a sleek cocktail lounge in 2016, Milwaukee revolted and it stayed as it was.
bars.vibe: Candlelit Black Forest tavern. Quiet enough to talk, serious enough about beer to matter, and open until 2:30 AM Friday and Saturday.
bars.signature_drink: A half-liter of Spaten or Franziskaner Weissbier; the Jagertee in cold weather
bars.wsp_fan_note: Not a fan bar. Landmark Lanes (bowling, three bars, arcade, open until 2 AM) is directly across the street if the night wants to keep going.

neighborhoods.name: Westown / Downtown West
neighborhoods.what: The west bank of the Milwaukee River along Wisconsin Avenue: the Riverside Theater, the old Grand Avenue retail spine (now 3rd Street Market Hall), Old World Third Street's German holdouts, and the Deer District to the north. The hotel and the show are both here.
neighborhoods.why: Everything for the run is here: the free Wolph street party outside the theater at 5:30 PM, Mo's after-parties next door, and a 10-minute radius that includes Mader's, Usinger's, Gertie the Duck on the bridge and the Bronze Fonz on the Riverwalk.

landmarks.name: Riverside Theater
landmarks.blurb: A 2,480-seat 1928 vaudeville-and-movie palace by Kirchhoff & Rose, tucked under the 12-story Empire Building that RKO built. Panic has played it since 2006 and done three-night fall stands here most years since 2008. Locals treat the run like a holiday.

landmarks.name: Gertie the Duck statue
landmarks.address: Wisconsin Avenue Bridge (northwest corner), Milwaukee, WI 53203
landmarks.blurb: In April 1945 a mallard nested on a piling under this bridge and a war-weary country followed her ducklings in the newspaper. Gwendolyn Gillen's bronze Gertie and her brood have sat on the bridge since 1997, about 150 feet from the Riverside marquee.

landmarks.name: The Bronze Fonz
landmarks.address: Milwaukee RiverWalk, just south of E Wells St (east bank), Milwaukee, WI 53202
landmarks.blurb: Henry Winkler's Fonzie in bronze, double thumbs up, unveiled in 2008 with most of the Happy Days cast present. Two blocks from the theater on the Riverwalk. The obligatory Milwaukee selfie.

landmarks.name: Usinger's Famous Sausage
landmarks.address: 1030 N Old World 3rd St (N Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr), Milwaukee, WI 53203
landmarks.blurb: Sausage-makers since 1880, in a shop with hand-painted elf murals, directly across from Mader's. A snack-size bratwurst or summer sausage travels well to a hotel room, and they ship.

landmarks.name: St. James 1868
landmarks.blurb: A deconsecrated 1868 Episcopal church turned event space, 10 minutes west on Wisconsin Avenue. On Sunday Oct 25 it hosts 'Candlelight: A Haunted Evening of Halloween Classics' at 4:30 PM and 6:45 PM. The 4:30 show ends in time for the 6:30 doors.

neighborhoods.name: East Town
neighborhoods.what: The east bank between the river and the lake: City Hall's 1895 Flemish tower, the Pfister Hotel, Cathedral Square, the Milwaukee Art Museum's white Calatrava wings on the waterfront, and the Water Street bar strip to the north.
neighborhoods.why: Five minutes across the Wisconsin Avenue bridge and the mood shifts from theater marquee to limestone and lake. Blu at the Pfister is here, as is the SafeHouse (on the Front Street alley on the east bank). Water Street bars are the loud, young, World Series-crowd zone, and the Halloween 'Boos Fest' crawl starts there Saturday.

image.credit: Gillfoto, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

landmarks.name: Milwaukee City Hall
landmarks.blurb: The 1895 Flemish Renaissance tower that was briefly among the tallest buildings in America, and the one in the Laverne & Shirley opening credits. The lobby in daytime is worth the detour: an eight-story open atrium ringed with iron railings, one of the great civic interiors in the Midwest.

landmarks.name: Pabst Theater
landmarks.blurb: Captain Frederick Pabst's 1895 opera house, sister venue to the Riverside, and the meeting point for the 'Shadow of City Hall' ghost walk (select Fri/Sat 7:30 PM, $33.57, ~2 hours, covering the Pfister ghost, City Hall and the Newhall House fire site).

landmarks.name: Milwaukee Art Museum (Quadracci Pavilion)
landmarks.address: 700 N Art Museum Dr, Milwaukee, WI 53202
landmarks.blurb: Santiago Calatrava's 2001 pavilion with the Burke Brise Soleil, a 217-foot pair of wings that open in the morning and fold at night (and close automatically if wind tops 23 mph).

landmarks.name: Brothers Bar & Grill (Boos Fest Halloween Crawl check-in)
landmarks.blurb: Starting point for the Saturday Oct 24 'Boos Fest' Halloween bar crawl (doors 6 PM, late check-in by 8 PM, GA $24.99 advance / $40 door) that works through Water Street and Old World Third. A college-crowd crawl, not a quality-bar crawl, but the costumes on Water Street Saturday night will be a show of their own.

neighborhoods.name: Historic Third Ward
neighborhoods.what: Milwaukee's old warehouse district south of I-794, now the gallery, boutique and restaurant quarter: Cream City brick, the Milwaukee Public Market, the Riverwalk, the Broadway Theatre Center, and the Hop streetcar running down Broadway and Milwaukee Street.
neighborhoods.why: The best daytime wander within 10 minutes of the hotel, and this weekend it hosts the Brewers World Series block party (Saturday, noon-11 PM, Menomonee St between Broadway and Milwaukee St, with big screens at Catalano Square). The Nightmare Bar horror pop-up at Pearl & Cade runs here too.

image.credit: SecretName101, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

landmarks.name: Milwaukee Public Market
landmarks.blurb: Indoor market hall with St. Paul Fish Company's lobster rolls and oyster bar, a cheese counter, Thief Wine's bar upstairs, and plenty of grab-and-go for the hotel. The Panic-weekend lunch stop in every fan guide since 2014.

landmarks.name: Catalano Square (World Series block party screens)
landmarks.address: Menomonee St & N Broadway, Milwaukee, WI 53202
landmarks.blurb: Sat Oct 24, noon-11 PM: Third Ward Beer Garden and the Historic Third Ward Association close Menomonee Street for food trucks, big screens showing Game 2, Brewers cocktails, and a live taping of the Foul Territory podcast 5-7 PM. The city's first World Series in 44 years, so the pregame energy around 5 PM will be something.

landmarks.name: Pearl & Cade (The Nightmare Bar pop-up)
landmarks.blurb: Fever's ticketed horror-themed pop-up bar in the Phoenix Building, Oct 8-31: 90-minute sessions at 7 PM and 9 PM, 21+, $17.50 with a welcome drink, costumes encouraged. Both sessions overlap the show, so it is a Monday-afternoon curiosity at most, barring a skipped set break.

landmarks.name: The Outsider (Kimpton Journeyman rooftop)
landmarks.blurb: Ninth-floor rooftop bar over the Third Ward with fire pits and a skyline view. A golden-hour stop (sunset is about 5:55 PM) before the 12-minute walk north to the street party. Hours not verified for this weekend, so check before going.

neighborhoods.name: Deer District
neighborhoods.what: The entertainment plaza around Fiserv Forum (Bucks arena, 2018) north of the theater district: a 30-acre district of bars, restaurants, and the big outdoor plaza famous for its 2021 NBA Finals watch parties.
neighborhoods.why: Ten minutes north on Vel R. Phillips Avenue. Brewers games are at American Family Field (4 miles west), not here, but the downtown sports bars will be heaving during Games 1 and 2. For a craft-cocktail person it is mostly a see-it-and-move-on.

image.credit: Fleyzk, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

landmarks.name: Fiserv Forum
landmarks.address: 1111 Vel R. Phillips Ave, Milwaukee, WI 53203
landmarks.blurb: Home of the Bucks, with a swooping zinc roof. The Bucks moved their home-opener tipoff this week so it would not collide with the Brewers' World Series run. That is how much this city is living baseball right now.

neighborhoods.name: Brady Street / Lower East Side
neighborhoods.what: Milwaukee's old Italian-and-Polish immigrant street turned bohemian bar-and-restaurant strip, running from the river east to Lake Drive, with Wolski's tucked two blocks off it and Von Trier and Landmark Lanes at the North Avenue end.
neighborhoods.why: This is where to go for character after the show: corner taverns, late hours (2:30 AM Fri/Sat), Glorioso's Italian deli for a daytime sandwich, and Brady's street Halloween party, which in 2026 lands on Halloween itself, Oct 31, after the trip. The weekend before should be festive rather than chaotic.

landmarks.name: Glorioso's Italian Market
landmarks.blurb: Family-run Italian grocery and deli since 1946, the anchor of Brady Street. The Italian sub and the cannoli are the move for a Saturday or Sunday lunch before a stroll.

landmarks.name: Landmark Lanes
landmarks.blurb: A subterranean 1927 bowling alley under the Oriental Theatre with three bars, a retro arcade, pool and darts. 21+ after 9 PM, bar open until 2 AM nightly, bowling until 11 PM. Directly across from Von Trier.

landmarks.name: Lakefront Brewery
landmarks.blurb: The most fun brewery tour in America, in an old riverside power plant across the river from Brady Street: 50 minutes, four 8-oz pours, a souvenir pint glass and a free-beer coupon good at local bars, $16 Sat-Sun. The beer hall has Bernie Brewer's original chalet from County Stadium. Tours run roughly every 30 minutes Sat noon-6 PM, Sun noon and 2 PM. The beer hall closes 9 PM (5 PM Sunday).

neighborhoods.name: Walker's Point
neighborhoods.what: The near-south-side neighborhood across the Menomonee River: Milwaukee's oldest settlement, now its densest cluster of distilleries, breweries, cocktail bars and chef-driven restaurants, with the Allen-Bradley clock watching over all of it.
neighborhoods.why: A 20-minute walk (or 6-minute ride) south reaches Boone & Crockett's river patio, Great Lakes Distillery, and Bryant's a little farther out. The Harley-Davidson Museum sits on the way at the river's edge.

landmarks.name: Allen-Bradley Clock Tower (the 'Polish Moon')
landmarks.blurb: Dedicated on Halloween 1962, with four faces more than 40 feet across. It was the largest four-faced clock in the world until Mecca's Abraj Al Bait topped it. South-siders call the glowing faces the Polish Moon. Visible from Blu's windows and from most of Walker's Point.

landmarks.name: Harley-Davidson Museum
landmarks.blurb: Twenty acres on the Menomonee River telling the story that began in a 10-by-15-foot Davidson-family shed in 1903. Non-riders go for the Engine Room and the 'tsunami bike' that washed up in Canada. A 15-minute walk from the Riverside, and the MOTOR bar and restaurant does a solid lunch.

landmarks.name: Basilica of St. Josaphat
landmarks.blurb: Polish immigrants built this 1901 basilica, dome 214 feet high, out of the demolished Chicago federal post office, which their pastor bought for $20,000 and shipped north on 500 railroad flatcars. Ten minutes south of Bryant's by car, an easy pairing with cocktails there.

neighborhoods.name: Bay View
neighborhoods.what: A lakeside neighborhood three miles south along Kinnickinnic Avenue: former ironworkers' village, now the city's most livable bar-and-restaurant strip, with mid-century lounges, record stores and coffee roasters.
neighborhoods.why: Worth the 12-minute rideshare for one evening: At Random's ice-cream cocktails and Lost Whale's Black Lagoon Halloween pop-up are a 5-minute walk apart, and Burnhearts is a fan-guide favorite dive nearby. Holler House, the oldest sanctioned bowling lanes in America, is a little west.

landmarks.name: Burnhearts
landmarks.blurb: A Bay View corner bar with a serious craft-beer list and a pinball corner, named 'my favorite bar in Milwaukee' in the 2015 Panic fan guide. Two blocks from At Random. Hours not verified for this weekend.

landmarks.name: Holler House
landmarks.blurb: A 1908 tavern whose two basement lanes are the oldest sanctioned tenpin lanes in the United States, still set by human pinsetters. Hundreds of signed bras hang from the ceiling, a tradition the late owner Marcy Skowronski started one rowdy night. Call ahead for lane time, and cash is wise.

the_hop.what: Free streetcar. No ticket, no app.
the_hop.route_notes: Two lines since Sept 1, 2026. The M-Line runs 2.1 miles from the Intermodal Station (Amtrak) through the Historic Third Ward, up Milwaukee St / Broadway through East Town to Burns Commons at the foot of Brady Street's east end. The L-Line links the Third Ward and downtown to the lakefront (Couture / Art Museum area). Transfer at the Wisconsin Avenue or City Hall stops. The nearest stop to the Riverside is 'Wisconsin Avenue' at N Milwaukee St, about a 6-minute walk east across the bridge. Useful for the Third Ward, the Public Market, the lakefront and the Pfister. Useless for Brady Street proper, Walker's Point and Bay View.
the_hop.hours: Mon-Fri 5:00 AM - midnight; Sat 7:00 AM - midnight; Sun 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM; every 15-20 minutes. It stops running before the show lets out, so it is a daytime and pre-show tool only.

getting_around.rideshare: Uber and Lyft are plentiful downtown. Expect surge pricing at ~11:30 PM Saturday and Sunday when the Riverside empties, and heavy demand Saturday after the 7 PM World Series game ends (~10:30 PM). Typical non-surge fares: downtown to Bay View or Bryant's $12-18, downtown to the airport roughly $16-20 (getridewise.com estimate, before surge, tolls and tip). Walk one block off Wisconsin Avenue to set a pickup pin. The block in front of the theater will be a mess.
getting_around.bublr_bikes: Bublr is Milwaukee's bike-share, with docks across downtown, the Third Ward, Brady Street and Bay View, pay-per-ride in the Bublr app. Mild weather this weekend (highs 66-69) makes a daytime ride along the lakefront path to the Art Museum pleasant. Hours and pricing not verified for this weekend: https://bublrbikes.org/

airport.name: Milwaukee Mitchell International (MKE)
options: Rideshare: ~8 miles, ~20 minutes, roughly $16-20 non-surge (getridewise.com estimate); pickup downtown anywhere, drop at Ticketing.

MCTS bus: the GreenLine runs from downtown to the airport (stop on the Baggage roadway island outside Exit 2); Route 80 also connects downtown to the airport (Ticketing curb). Adult fare $2.75 in 2026, ~30-40 minutes. Catch the GreenLine along Wisconsin Ave / Water St; check ridemcts.com for the stop nearest the hotel.

Amtrak Hiawatha stops at the Milwaukee Airport Rail Station (5601 S 6th St) with a free 24-hour shuttle to the terminal, but it is a Chicago-bound train. From downtown it is a roundabout option and the airport station is under construction. Not recommended.
airport.monday_3pm_flight_leave_by: Leave downtown by 12:30 PM (arrive ~12:50 PM, two hours before a 3:00 PM domestic departure, with cushion). MKE is a small, fast airport, so 12:45 PM is still comfortable with TSA PreCheck.

fun_facts.fact: The Bronze Fonz on the Riverwalk, two blocks from the Riverside, was unveiled in 2008 with most of the Happy Days cast watching. Visit Milwaukee raised about $75,000-85,000 to cast it after locals vetoed its planned spot at Wisconsin and Water.

Milwaukee's downtown bridges cross the river at odd angles because of the Bridge War of 1845, when rival founders Solomon Juneau (east bank) and Byron Kilbourn (west bank) laid out street grids that deliberately did not line up, and residents tore down each other's bridges. The three settlements merged into one city in January 1846.

In April 1945 a mallard named Gertie nested on a piling under the Wisconsin Avenue bridge, and the whole country followed her story in the newspapers as the war ended. Her bronze statue has sat on the bridge, steps from the Riverside marquee, since 1997.

The Allen-Bradley clock in Walker's Point, dedicated on Halloween 1962 with faces more than 40 feet across, was the largest four-faced clock on Earth until Mecca's Abraj Al Bait tower passed it. South-siders call it the Polish Moon.
The Milwaukee Art Museum's Burke Brise Soleil, designed by Santiago Calatrava, spreads 217 feet of white 'wings' every morning and folds them at night. Sensors close them if the wind tops 23 mph.
Milwaukee is 'Cream City' because of its bricks: the local red clay is so rich in lime and sulfur that it fires to a pale cream-yellow. It is all over the Third Ward and Walker's Point.
The first commercially successful typewriter came out of a Milwaukee machine shop, developed by Christopher Latham Sholes (patent June 23, 1868). Its keyboard became QWERTY.
Harley-Davidson was born in Milwaukee in 1903, when William Harley and the Davidson brothers built their first motorcycle in a 10-by-15-foot backyard shed.

'Brew City' earned its name: Milwaukee was once home to four of the world's largest breweries at once, Schlitz, Blatz, Pabst and Miller. Only Miller still brews here. Carl Schurz called the city the 'German Athens of America' in the 1850s.
Summerfest, on the lakefront each June and July since 1968, was certified by Guinness World Records in 1999 as the world's largest music festival. The 2001 edition drew over a million people.

The Pfister Hotel (1893) is said to be haunted by its founder's son Charles Pfister, who died in 1927. Visiting Major League players including Bryce Harper, Giancarlo Stanton and Ji-Man Choi have reported moved furniture and spirits in their rooms, and some refuse to stay there.
The SafeHouse spy bar takes a password at the door. Without it, 'Agent Moneypenny' runs a 'clearance test' of silly antics, broadcast live to everyone already drinking inside.
Holler House, a 1908 south-side tavern, has the two oldest sanctioned tenpin bowling lanes in America, still reset by human pinsetters, and a ceiling hung with nearly a thousand signed bras.
Liberace, the rhinestoned king of Las Vegas, was born Wladziu Valentino Liberace in West Allis, a Milwaukee suburb, in 1919.

The Basilica of St. Josaphat (1901) was built by Polish immigrants out of the demolished Chicago federal post office, which the pastor bought as salvage for $20,000 and hauled north on 500 railroad flatcars.

The Riverside Theater opened April 29, 1928 as a 2,480-seat vaudeville and movie house, tucked beneath the 12-story Empire Building that RKO Pictures commissioned. Widespread Panic has played it since 2006.

weather_and_packing.typical_late_october: Highs in the mid-50s and lows in the high 30s are normal, with the lake keeping downtown a few degrees milder than the suburbs. This weekend is running well above normal and dry.

forecast_this_weekend.mon: Mostly cloudy and cooler, high 59, NE wind 10-15 mph
forecast_this_weekend.precip: No measurable rain in the NWS forecast through Monday; first chance is Wednesday night.

packing_tips: Hi Baby, pack a real jacket for the walk out at 11:30 PM. It will be around 50 degrees and breezier near the river.
Layers for the street party: 5:30 PM is sunny-and-66 going to dusk-and-55 within the hour, with sunset about 5:55 PM.
Comfortable shoes. Everything worth doing downtown is a 5-25 minute walk and the Riverwalk is uneven brick in spots.
A small purse only. The Riverside allows bags no larger than 13 x 4 x 9 inches, no backpacks, no bag check.
Cash. Wolski's is cash only, and small taverns and the tip jars at the street party prefer it.
Anything Halloween-ish. Saturday night downtown will be full of costumes.

safety_and_practical.note: Wisconsin Avenue, Water Street, the Riverwalk and the Third Ward are busy and well lit until bar time, and this weekend they will be unusually crowded with Panic fans and World Series revelers, which helps. Standard big-city sense applies: stay on Wisconsin Ave / Water St / Milwaukee St rather than cutting through the parking structures or the quieter blocks west of 6th St, and take a rideshare rather than walking to Brady Street, Walker's Point or Bay View after dark. Panhandling near the Riverside and the Grand Avenue block is common and generally harmless.

No pharmacy in downtown proper is open overnight. The nearest 24-hour store is the Walgreens at Brady & Farwell (store open 24 hours, pharmacy counter opens 8 AM). The Walgreens at 275 W Wisconsin Ave, half a block from the Riverside, is a convenience store without a pharmacy (opens 7 AM). The nearest 24-hour pharmacy counter is Walgreens 4296 S 76th St, Greenfield, about 20 minutes by car.

location.name: Walgreens (24-hour store), Brady & Farwell
location.blurb: Open 24 hours for Advil, water, snacks and phone chargers. Pharmacy counter 8 AM. Phone 414-272-2171. About a 7-minute rideshare from the hotel.

safety_and_practical.note: The nearest walk-in urgent care to downtown with weekend hours is Aurora Urgent Care at Schlitz Park, about a mile north of the Riverside (5-minute rideshare). Hours per a third-party directory: Mon-Fri 8 AM - 8 PM, Sat-Sun 8 AM - 4 PM. Call 414-276-4242 to confirm. For anything serious, Aurora Sinai Medical Center ER (945 N 12th St) and Ascension Columbia St. Mary's ER (2301 N Lake Dr) are both under 10 minutes by car. Call 911 for emergencies.

location.name: Aurora Urgent Care, Schlitz Park
location.blurb: Walk-in urgent care in the old Schlitz brewery complex. Weekend hours 8 AM - 4 PM per directory listing. Confirm by phone, 414-276-4242.

safety_and_practical.note: Cards work nearly everywhere downtown, in the Third Ward and at the breweries. Old-school taverns are the exception: Wolski's is cash only, and some Brady Street and south-side bars (Thurman's 15, Holler House) are cash or cash-preferred. The street party and after-parties will have card readers, but the tip jars want cash. ATMs sit inside most bars with a $3-4 fee.

Standard American norms: $1-2 per beer or simple drink, 20% on cocktails and tabs, 18-20% at restaurants, 15-20% for rideshare. Bryant's adds 20% automatically for parties of six or more. Brewery tour guides appreciate a few dollars.

State law sets closing statewide and cities cannot change it: bars must close 2:00-6:00 AM Monday through Friday, and 2:30-6:00 AM on Saturday and Sunday mornings. In practice Friday night and Saturday night last call is 2:30 AM, and Sunday night last call is 2:00 AM (it becomes Monday). Many bars close earlier, so the hours listed for each bar are the ones that matter. Package liquor and wine sales stop at 9 PM statewide, beer at midnight or earlier by local rule. Drinking age is 21 and IDs are checked at the door after 9-10 PM almost everywhere.

Doors 6:30 PM, show 8:00 PM all three nights. Arrive 30 minutes before you want to be seated to clear security. Bags no larger than 13 x 4 x 9 inches, no backpacks, no bag storage, no outside food or water. The Riverside's beer selection is good and reasonably priced (Pabst Theater Group makes a point of it), and the basement bathrooms got an $800,000 renovation, so the lines are better than they used to be.

Game 2 is at American Family Field (4 miles west) at 7:00 PM Saturday, the Brewers' first World Series in 44 years. Downtown sports bars will be at capacity from late afternoon, Water Street will be rowdy after the game ends around 10:30 PM, and rideshare surge will overlap with the Riverside letting out. Game 3 is Monday night in Tampa, so Monday is calm.
